The thing that caught us during the naive implementation was needing to "pause" execution at state root calculation when data is missing, compared to the more obvious need to pause during the generic EVM execution.

excerpts.author: tkstanczak

excerpts.author: tkstanczak
excerpts.content: BeamDb simply is slow to request some data

excerpts.author: tkstanczak
excerpts.content: but from the EVM perspective it behaves exactly the same

excerpts.author: tkstanczak
excerpts.content: just like a very slow database

excerpts.author: tkstanczak
excerpts.content: so evm does not have any code changes for beam sync

excerpts.author: jason.carver
excerpts.content: we patch in at the state accessors underneath the EVM, and catch the exception about missing data. then we don't return until the data is available. So from the EVMs point of view, the data access is just reaaally slow
